page: Amazon Web Services c4.large is a fourth-generation compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Xen hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it utilizes a dedicated 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor featuring 1 physical core hyperthreaded into 2 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a 25 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2, though it lacks newer AVX-512 and AMX vector extensions. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, maintaining a traditional compute-oriented 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes a 1 Gbps baseline network interface, no bundled local storage, and zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements place the single-core CPU throughput of the c4.large in the middle tier, recording 1478.68 in single-core stress-ng tests. However, overall multi-core and memory throughput reflect the constraints of a single physical core on older microarchitecture. Multi-core stress-ng performance scores 1945.19, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations reach 1133.0 and 1368.0 respectively. Memory bandwidth registers at 13.03 GB/sec for uncached reads and 11.47 GB/sec for uncached writes, resulting in a PassMark memory score of 883.54. Synthetic database tasks achieve 709.82 operations in PassMark, Redis SET benchmarks process 0.87 million operations per second, and static web serving delivers 1.98 GB/sec.

The primary operational tradeoff of the c4.large is its reliance on earlier-generation Haswell-era silicon and the absence of ephemeral NVMe storage. Because persistent storage relies entirely on external network volumes, I/O-intensive workloads may encounter latency boundaries compared to newer generations. Nevertheless, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution for smaller-footprint services without CPU credit exhaustion risks. The instance profile is suited for light front-end web serving, continuous integration build workers, basic batch processing, and non-critical utility microservices that do not require high memory density or advanced vector compute instructions.
description: Amazon Web Services c4.large is a fourth-generation compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor configured with 1 physical core and 2 virtual CPUs. The instance includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Local storage is not provided, requiring attached network storage for data persistence. Benchmark results indicate moderate single-threaded performance, achieving 1478.68 in stress-ng single-core testing, but multi-core throughput, memory bandwidth, and overall compute scores fall into lower comparative tiers due to the dual-thread single-core hardware profile. Without integrated GPU acceleration or local disk, the instance presents low entry-level operational costs for older generation hardware, making it suitable for lightweight compute-bound processing, basic web serving, staging environments, and legacy batch tasks.
